newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: BOMBERS BLAST COLOMBIAN GOALIE'S HOME.
newsitem.headline: BOMBERS BLAST COLOMBIAN GOALIE'S HOME.

text.p: Unidentified attackers bombed the home of Colombian goalkeeper Rene Higuita, causing property damage but no injuries, police said on Monday.

Higuita, a flamboyant figure in Colombia's soccer team in the 1994 World Cup finals, was out when the bomb exploded at his house in the northwest city of Medellin on Sunday evening. Police said intruders forced their way past the maid into the house and detonated a charge of dynamite, which damaged windows, doors and furniture. They gave no motives for the attack.

Higuita quit Medellin side Atletico Nacional at the start of November and has not played since. He was until then one of the country's most popular sporting figures, known for his lion-like mane of black hair and his ability to thrill fans with incredible saves and dashing forays from the goal area.
He declined to join the national squad for qualifying matches for the 1998 World Cup, saying he was playing badly and needed a break.
